messages:
maya: FYI — Elliott from AcmeCorp is stuck during onboarding. They completed SSO, invited their engineer, but the Console shows no API key and their app gets 401s. Pasting customer-provided repro and screenshots.

maya: customer says they clicked "Create API Key" in the console but the modal completes without an obvious key in the UI. They get an email confirmation though.

maya: customer error from their curl test: 
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME-xxxx" -d '{"input":"hi"}' -i
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{"error":"api_key_not_found"}
```

maya: they shared a screenshot of the Console > Projects list showing their new project name (acme-inference) but no keys listed under Project Settings -> API Keys. Screenshot shows toast: "API key created" immediately after creation.

provisioning-bot: Automated note: new_api_key event: user_id=elliott@acmecorp, project_id=p-98321, key_id=k_7f3b, created_at=2026-02-12T16:22:13Z

alex: thanks — tagging infra-ops. @infra-ops any chance the key was created but attached to a different project id? Iirc we've had a mapping race where SSO linkage finishes slightly after key provisioning.

infra-ops: looking. Running quick lookup: `SELECT project_id, visible_in_console FROM api_keys WHERE key_id='k_7f3b';` returns `project_id = p-19832`, `visible_in_console = false` for that key_id.

infra-ops: looks like the key was created but correlated to the wrong project (p-19832). That project belongs to a sandbox account created during an earlier trial webhook flow.

jamie: ugh — repro steps look like race between oauth callback and provisioning service. We saw a similar race in Feb where the session cookie pointed to the wrong org if the user had a stale cookie.

alex: can we do two things: 1) re-point the key to the correct project (p-98321) in the DB and flip visible_in_console=true, 2) check audit trail to ensure the customer doesn't actually have two active keys? If safe, rotate/regenerate the key and email Elliott the new secret.

infra-ops: SQL patch ready, will run after QA signoff: 
```
BEGIN;
UPDATE api_keys SET project_id='p-98321', visible_in_console=true WHERE key_id='k_7f3b' AND project_id='p-19832';
-- verify no duplicate keys in p-98321 with same fingerprint
COMMIT;
```

maya: customer ok with key rotation. They prefer a fresh key and clear repro steps so their devs can continue. Could we also flag the provisioning flow to avoid creating keys before org finalization?

jamie: I'll open a follow-up ticket in eng-runtime for the race. For now infra-ops, run the patch and then trigger a key rotate job which will create sk-ACME-NEW and invalidate k_7f3b. We'll then send the new secret to Elliott via secure email.

infra-ops: patch applied at 16:37Z, rotate job queued. Confirmed in DB: `project_id='p-98321', visible_in_console=true` for k_7f3b and rotate created k_ab12 (staging secret).

provisioning-bot: Key rotation completed: old_key=k_7f3b disabled, new_key=k_ab12 active, created_at=2026-02-12T16:40:21Z

maya: sent secure email to elliott@acmecorp with new key and steps. Asked them to test and report back.

maya: suggested temporary workaround in case others hit this: use Console -> Organization -> API Keys (admin) to confirm key visibility; if missing, ping support with your project_id and key_id from provisioning webhook.

alex: opened ENG-1238 to harden the SSO/provisioning ordering; added regression test that uses a delayed oauth callback.

maya: customer confirmed at 16:45Z that their curl test now returns 200 and tokens are valid: 
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME-NEW" -d '{"input":"hi"}' -i
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{"output":"hello"}
```

maya: resolved with customer; leaving thread open for ENG-1238 tracking. :white_check_mark:
